info.title: RESOURCES
info.description:
# Hyperwallet Documentation

This collection provides a comprehensive set of API requests for integrating with the **Hyperwallet/Paylution** payout platform. It enables programmatic management of users, transfer methods, payments, and related resources.

## Purpose

Hyperwallet is a global payout platform that allows businesses to disburse funds to recipients worldwide. This collection covers the core REST API endpoints for:

- Creating and managing payout recipients (users)

- Configuring transfer methods (bank accounts, bank cards, prepaid cards, Venmo, crypto, etc.)

- Initiating and tracking payments and transfers

- Handling status transitions and compliance workflows


## Main Resource Groups

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Users** | Create, retrieve, update users and their status transitions |
| **Bank Accounts** | Manage bank account transfer methods for direct deposit or wire |
| **Bank Cards** | Register and manage debit/credit cards for payouts |
| **Prepaid Cards** | Issue and manage prepaid cards, balances, and receipts |
| **Venmo Accounts** | Link and manage Venmo as a payout method |
| **Crypto Accounts** | Configure cryptocurrency wallets for payouts |
| **Wallet Accounts** | Manage Hyperwallet wallet balances |
| **Payments** | Create payments, track status, and manage supplemental data |
| **Transfers** | Initiate transfers between accounts, including refunds |
| **Business Stakeholders** | Manage stakeholders for business profiles |

## Security Model (JWS / JWE)

All requests in this collection use **JSON Web Signature (JWS)** and **JSON Web Encryption (JWE)** for secure communication:

1. **JWS (Signing)**: Request payloads are signed using your private signing key (`PRIVATE_JWK` or `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` environment variable) with RS256 algorithm.

2. **JWE (Encryption)**: The signed payload is then encrypted using Hyperwallet's public encryption key (fetched from `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL`).

3. **Response Decryption**: Responses are decrypted and stored in `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` environment variable for validation.


## Environment Configuration

Set the following variables in your Postman environment:

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `base_url` | API base URL (e.g., `https://api.paylution.com/rest/v4`) |
| `PRIVATE_JWK` | Your private JWK for signing requests (JSON format) |
| `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` | Alternative signing key (if separate from encryption) |
| `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` | URL to fetch Hyperwallet's public JWKS (defaults to `https://api.paylution.com/jwkset`) |

## Running Requests

1. **Select an environment** with the required variables configured.

2. **Open any request** in the collection.

3. **Send the request** — the pre-request script automatically handles JWS signing and JWE encryption.

4. **View results** — check the `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` environment variable or the Visualizer tab for the decrypted response.

5. **Run tests** — post-response scripts validate status codes, payload structure, and key fields.


## Collection Runner

Use the Postman Collection Runner to execute multiple requests in sequence. The collection-level scripts ensure consistent JWS/JWE handling and response validation across all requests.

get.description:
You can retrieve a list of users belonging to your program by sending a GET request to the /users endpoint.

Listing Users Corresponding to a Program

Overview  
Retrieve users from Hyperwallet/Paylution associated with your program. Supports rich filtering, sorting, and pagination. Responses are JOSE-encoded (JWE payload, JWS signature) as per Hyperwallet security requirements.

Endpoint  
GET {{base_url}}/users

Headers

- Content-Type: application/jose+json

- Accept: application/jose+json


Authentication & Security

- Requests are signed (JWS) and encrypted (JWE) using your program keys.

- This request’s pre-request script prepares the JWS/JWE. Ensure these environment variables exist:

    - PRIVATE_JWK, PRIVATE_JWK_SIG

    - HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL (optional; defaults to [https://api.paylution.com/jwkset](https://api.paylution.com/jwkset))


Query Parameters  
All parameters are optional unless noted. Use only those relevant to your filter.

- clientUserId (string)

- createdBefore (ISO8601 datetime)

- createdAfter (ISO8601 datetime)

- email (string)

- programToken (string)

- status (string)

- verificationStatus (string; allowed values: NOT_REQUIRED, REQUIRED, UNDER_REVIEW, VERIFIED)

- taxVerificationStatus (string; allowed values: NOT_REQUIRED, REQUIRED, FAILED, UNDER_REVIEW, VERIFIED, READY_FOR_REVIEW. Note: FAILED is a temporary status before changing to REQUIRED.)

- businessStakeholderVerificationStatus (string; allowed values: NOT_REQUIRED, REQUIRED, FAILED, UNDER_REVIEW, VERIFIED, READY_FOR_REVIEW. Note: FAILED is a temporary status before changing to REQUIRED.)

- letterOfAuthorizationStatus (string; allowed values: NOT_REQUIRED, REQUIRED, FAILED, UNDER_REVIEW, VERIFIED, READY_FOR_REVIEW. Note: FAILED is a temporary status before changing to REQUIRED.)

- createdOn (ISO8601 date)

- profileType (string; allowed values: INDIVIDUAL, BUSINESS)

- firstName, middleName, lastName (string)

- dateOfBirth (YYYY-MM-DD)

- countryOfBirth, countryOfNationality (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)

- phoneNumber, mobileNumber (E.164)

- governmentId (string)

- governmentIdType (string)

- passportId, driversLicenseId, employerId (string)

- addressLine1, addressLine2, city, stateProvince, country, postalCode (string; country = ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)

- language (ISO 639-1)

- businessType (string)

- businessName, businessRegistrationId, businessRegistrationStateProvince, businessRegistrationCountry, businessOperatingName (string)


### Example requests

Minimal list (no filters, default limit):

``` http
GET {{base_url}}/users

 ```

List individual users by email:

``` http
GET {{base_url}}/users?profileType=INDIVIDUAL&email=test.user@example.com

 ```

List users by verification and tax verification status:

``` http
GET {{base_url}}/users?verificationStatus=UNDER_REVIEW&taxVerificationStatus=READY_FOR_REVIEW

 ```

Combined filters (program, profile type, status, and verification flags):

``` http
GET {{base_url}}/users?programToken=prg-14b739d1-2bd5-4879-9a1c-ec3421c77d42&profileType=INDIVIDUAL&status=ACTIVATED&verificationStatus=VERIFIED&taxVerificationStatus=VERIFIED&businessStakeholderVerificationStatus=VERIFIED

 ```

### Common filter patterns

| Use case | Key params | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filter by exact email | `email` | `GET {{base_url}}/users?email=test.user@example.com` |
| Filter by client user id | `clientUserId` | `GET {{base_url}}/users?clientUserId=t-1707994378490` |
| Filter by profile type | `profileType` (`INDIVIDUAL` or `BUSINESS`) | `GET {{base_url}}/users?profileType=INDIVIDUAL` |
| Filter by creation date range | `createdAfter`, `createdBefore` (ISO8601) | `GET {{base_url}}/users?createdAfter=2024-01-01T00:00:00&createdBefore=2024-12-31T23:59:59` |
| Filter by verification flags | `verificationStatus`, `taxVerificationStatus` (for example `VERIFIED`, `READY_FOR_REVIEW`) | `GET {{base_url}}/users?verificationStatus=VERIFIED&taxVerificationStatus=READY_FOR_REVIEW` |

post.description:
**Purpose**

Create a Hyperwallet user (INDIVIDUAL or BUSINESS) by sending a JWS-signed and JWE-encrypted payload to the /users endpoint, aligned with the official Hyperwallet v4 **Create User** API.

Endpoint  
POST {{base_url}}/users

Method  
POST

Headers

- Content-Type: `application/jose+json`

- Accept: `application/jose+json`


Authentication and Crypto Prerequisites

This collection uses a JOSE-based integration pattern on top of the standard Hyperwallet Create User endpoint:

- Two-step cryptographic flow in the pre-request script:

    1. **JWS signing (RS256)** using your private JWK held in the environment.

    2. **JWE encryption (RSA-OAEP + A256GCM)** to the Hyperwallet public key fetched from JWKS.

- Required environment variables:

    - `base_url`: Base API URL (for example, `https://api.paylution.com/rest/v4`).

    - `PRIVATE_JWK`: Private JWK JSON string used for RS256 signing.

    - `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` (if applicable in your setup): Optional secondary signing material.

    - `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` (optional): JWKS endpoint for encryption key. Defaults to `https://api.paylution.com/jwkset`.

- No bearer tokens are added directly; the JOSE payload is the authorization mechanism expected by this collection’s examples.


Request Body

Body mode: **raw JSON**, which is transformed by the pre-request script into JWS, then JWE before sending.

Below is a concise summary of the core **Create User** fields, aligned with Hyperwallet’s v4 documentation for the `POST /users` endpoint. Unless indicated otherwise, fields are provided in the JSON body (not as query parameters).

### Core Identity & Program Fields

- **profileType** (string, **required**)

    - The user’s profile type.

    - Allowed values:

        - `INDIVIDUAL`

        - `BUSINESS`

    - Notes:

        - When `profileType = BUSINESS`, personal fields such as `firstName`, `middleName`, `lastName`, and `dateOfBirth` are ignored on this call. Use **Create Business Stakeholder** to add individual stakeholders for a business.


[... existing field documentation and minimal/rich JSON examples remain here ...]

### Common create patterns

The table below summarizes some typical **Create User** payload shapes you’re likely to use. These are conceptual groupings; exact fields and validation rules should follow Hyperwallet’s official API reference.

| Use case | Key fields (illustrative) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal INDIVIDUAL user | `clientUserId`, `profileType = INDIVIDUAL`, `programToken`, `email`, `country` | Smallest practical payload to register an individual user. Additional optional KYC fields (name, dateOfBirth, address) can be added later or in subsequent flows depending on your compliance requirements. |
| Minimal BUSINESS user | `clientUserId`, `profileType = BUSINESS`, `programToken`, `businessName`, `email`, `country` | Basic business onboarding when you only need to identify the legal entity and tie it to your program. Use **Create Business Stakeholder** APIs to add individuals linked to this business. |
| INDIVIDUAL with extended KYC info | All minimal INDIVIDUAL fields, plus `firstName`, `middleName` (optional), `lastName`, `dateOfBirth`, and address fields such as `addressLine1`, `city`, `stateProvince`, `country`, `postalCode` | Recommended pattern when you want to collect KYC-relevant information up front for individuals to reduce later remediation. Exact address requirements depend on the user’s country and program configuration. |
| BUSINESS with extended business data | All minimal BUSINESS fields, plus `businessType`, `businessRegistrationId`, `businessRegistrationCountry`, `businessOperatingName` (and optionally `businessRegistrationStateProvince`) | Use when you need richer business context for compliance or reporting. Some combinations of `businessType` and registration fields may be mandatory depending on jurisdiction and Hyperwallet configuration. |
| INDIVIDUAL with language and phone | Minimal INDIVIDUAL fields, plus `language`, and one or more phone-related fields such as `phoneNumber` and/or `mobileNumber` | Useful when you want to control communication preferences and have at least one reachable phone contact. `language` should follow the allowed language codes documented by Hyperwallet for your program. |

### Validation checklist (before sending)

- For all users: non-empty `clientUserId`, a valid `programToken`, a well-formed `email`, and a `country` using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (for example, `US`, `CA`, `DE`).

- For INDIVIDUAL users: `profileType = INDIVIDUAL` and at least basic name fields populated (for example, `firstName` and `lastName`) where your program or KYC rules require them.

- For BUSINESS users: `profileType = BUSINESS` and a non-empty `businessName`; include `businessType`, `businessRegistrationId`, `businessRegistrationCountry`, and `businessRegistrationStateProvince` where required by your program or local regulations.

- Optional but recommended: `dateOfBirth` for individuals, plus address fields such as `addressLine1`, `city`, `stateProvince`, and `postalCode` to support KYC and downstream compliance checks.

- If using `phoneNumber` or `mobileNumber`, send values in E.164 format where possible (for example, `+14155550123`).

- Confirm that your environment variables for JOSE are set and valid: `PRIVATE_JWK` (and `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` if applicable), `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` (or the default JWKS URL), and `base_url` for the correct environment.

get.description:
### Overview

Retrieve a single user resource by user-token from the Hyperwallet/Paylution API. This request is read-only.

### Method & URL

- GET {{base_url}}/users/:user-token


### Required headers

- Content-Type: application/jose+json

- Accept: application/jose+json


### Security

This request is prepared in the pre-request script using:

- JWS signature (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, SHA-256) with PRIVATE_JWK_SIG

- JWE encryption (RSA-OAEP, SHA-256) using the platform JWKS at {{HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL}} (or default [https://api.paylution.com/jwkset](https://api.paylution.com/jwkset))


Environment variables expected:

- base_url: API base URL

- PRIVATE_JWK, PRIVATE_JWK_SIG: client private keys for encryption/signing

- HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL (optional): JWKS endpoint for recipient public keys


### Path parameter

- :user-token (string) — The unique identifier of the user to fetch.


### Optional query parameters

The endpoint supports many filters; leave blank to fetch by token only. Common keys include: token, status, verificationStatus, taxVerificationStatus, businessStakeholderVerificationStatus, letterOfAuthorizationStatus, createdOn, clientUserId, profileType, firstName, middleName, lastName, dateOfBirth, countryOfBirth, countryOfNationality, phoneNumber, mobileNumber, email, governmentId, governmentIdType, passportId, driversLicenseId, employerId, addressLine1, addressLine2, city, stateProvince, country, postalCode, language, programToken, businessType, businessName, businessRegistrationId, businessRegistrationStateProvince, businessRegistrationCountry, businessOperatingName.

Reference requests with similar shapes: [/users/{user-token}](https://request/20632464-a5449a0f-8b61-4dcb-bf7c-eed112f64a6b), [/users/{user-token}](https://request/20632464-4239169e-a9d4-406d-9155-c0418c8e4300), [/users/{user-token}](https://request/20632464-88cdf91a-5464-4c65-85cc-a89496f9efb1).

### Scripts

- Pre-request: Builds JWS and JWE envelopes and sets JWE/JWS payload variables.

- Tests: Attempts to parse DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD and validates presence of links. Logs JWE/JWS when present.


### Example

GET {{base_url}}/users/usr-d787d153-045b-4ba3-925f-ebb538342a01  
Headers:  
Content-Type: application/jose+json  
Accept: application/jose+json

### Responses

- 200 OK — Encrypted response body; post-response script will decrypt and store as DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD.

- 4xx/5xx — Check signing/encryption configuration and required variables.


### Notes

- Do not edit this request’s method, URL, or headers when using this template—only adjust :user-token and filters as needed.

- Use the Production Paylution environment to resolve variables like base_url and key material.

put.description:
# Endpoint

Update user

- Method: PUT

- Path: /users/{user-token}

- Base URL: {{base_url}}


## Summary

Updates an existing user’s profile details in Hyperwallet/Paylution. The request payload is signed (JWS) and encrypted (JWE) per the pre-request script. The server expects application/jose+json content.

## Path variables

- user-token (required): The unique user token, e.g., usr-d787d153-045b-4ba3-925f-ebb538342a01


## Query parameters (optional)

These may be accepted by the upstream API but are typically omitted when updating. Leave blank to avoid sending them.

- clientUserId

- profileType

- businessStakeholderVerificationStatus

- firstName, middleName, lastName

- dateOfBirth

- countryOfBirth, countryOfNationality

- phoneNumber, mobileNumber, email

- governmentId, governmentIdType, passportId, driversLicenseId, employerId

- addressLine1, addressLine2, city, stateProvince, country, postalCode

- language

- programToken

- businessType, businessName, businessOperatingName

- businessRegistrationId, businessRegistrationStateProvince, businessRegistrationCountry


## Headers

- Content-Type: application/jose+json

- Accept: application/jose+json


## Authentication & Security

- Request body is signed (RS256) and then encrypted (RSA-OAEP-256 + AES-GCM) by the pre-request script using values from the active environment (e.g., PRIVATE_JWK, HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL).

- Ensure PRIVATE_JWK (and, if applicable, PRIVATE_JWK_SIG) is set in the active environment.


## Request body example (before signing/encryption)

``` json
{
  "email": "jim.432@company.com",
  "firstName": "Jim",
  "lastName": "Smithe"
}

 ```

## Success response

- Status: 200 OK

- Body: Encrypted JWE. The post-response script will attempt to decrypt and place the plaintext in the environment variable DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD.


## Tests & Scripts

- Pre-request: Builds JWS and JWE around the raw JSON body.

- Tests: Parses DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD and validates structure (e.g., presence of links) when available.


## Notes

- Use {{base_url}} to switch between environments.

- Examples are available under this request to demonstrate typical responses.[https://docs.hyperwallet.com/content/api/v4/overview/errors#ret](https://docs.hyperwallet.com/content/api/v4/overview/errors#retrieve-a-user%5BRead)([https://docs.hyperwallet.com/content/api](https://docs.hyperwallet.com/content/api/v4/overview/errors#retrieve-a-user)

Summary  
Retrieves bank accounts for a specific user in Hyperwallet/Paylution.

Request

- Method: GET

- URL template: {{base_url}}/users/{user-token}/bank-accounts

- Path variables:
    - user-token (string, required): Unique identifier of the user whose bank accounts are being retrieved.


Query parameters  
Provide any of the following as query string filters. All values are strings unless noted. Examples use realistic values; adjust as needed.

- :user-token (string) — Do not use in the query string; the user-token is a path variable. (Present in the autogenerated URL; ignore.)

- createdBefore (ISO 8601 datetime): e.g., 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z

- createdAfter (ISO 8601 datetime): e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z

- createdOn (ISO 8601 date): e.g., 2024-05-10

- type (string): Bank account type. e.g., "BANK_ACCOUNT"

- status (string): e.g., "ACTIVATED", "VERIFIED", "DEACTIVATED"

- sortBy (string): Field to sort by; use "createdOn" or other supported fields. Use prefix - for descending when applicable (see Notes). e.g., "createdOn"

- limit (integer as string): Page size. e.g., "20"

- token (string): Specific bank account token to fetch.

- transferMethodCurrency (string): ISO 4217, e.g., "USD"

- isDefaultTransferMethod (boolean as string): "true" or "false"

post.description:
## Overview
Creates a bank account transfer method for a Hyperwallet user. This request is JWS-signed and JWE-encrypted via the pre-request script and expects a JWE response.

- Method: POST
- URL: `{{base_url}}/users/:user-token/bank-accounts`
- Protocol: HTTP
- Auth: Handled by JWS (RS256) signing and JWE (RSA-OAEP-256 + AES-GCM) encryption in pre-request script.

## Path and Query Parameters
- `:user-token` (path/query): The Hyperwallet user token. In this request it is currently supplied as a query placeholder `:user-token=` in the URL.
- Supported query keys (from workspace references): `profileType`, `transferMethodCountry`, `transferMethodCurrency`, `type`, `branchId`, `bankAccountId`, `bankAccountPurpose`, `firstName`, `middleName`, `lastName`, `country`, `stateProvince`, `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`, `city`, `postalCode`.

## Required Headers
- `Content-Type: application/jose+json`
- `Accept: application/jose+json`

## Request Body
Content type: JSON (wrapped and transformed by the pre-request script into JWS + JWE).

Example body:
```json
{
  "profileType": "INDIVIDUAL",
  "transferMethodCountry": "US",
  "transferMethodCurrency": "USD",
  "type": "BANK_ACCOUNT",
  "branchId": "101089292",
  "bankAccountId": "7991012345",
  "bankAccountPurpose": "SAVINGS",
  "firstName": "John",
  "lastName": "Smith",
  "country": "US",
  "stateProvince": "WA",
  "addressLine1": "123 Main Street",
  "city": "Hometown",
  "postalCode": "12345",
  "bankAccountRelationship": "SELF"
}
```

Body schema (guide): `profileType: INDIVIDUAL`, `transferMethodCountry: US`, `transferMethodCurrency: USD`, `type: BANK_ACCOUNT`, bank and address fields as strings.

## Scripts
- Pre-request: Signs payload with RS256 using `PRIVATE_JWK` and encrypts using recipient JWKS at `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` (defaults to https://api.paylution.com/jwkset). Produces `JWS_PAYLOAD` and `JWE_PAYLOAD`.
- Tests (post-response): Decrypts response and stores it in `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD`; asserts presence of `token` and `createdOn`.

Environment variables used:
- `{{base_url}}` (URL base)
- `PRIVATE_JWK`, `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` (keys)
- Optional: `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` (JWKS endpoint)

## Responses
Common outcomes:
- `201 Created`: Bank account transfer method created. Decrypted payload typically includes `token`, `status`, `createdOn`, and `links`.
- `400 Bad Request`: Validation or schema errors.
- `401/403`: Auth/signature or encryption issues (verify keys and JWKS).
- `409 Conflict`: Duplicate bank account for user.

Saved examples:
- See saved responses under this request for variations: 
  - Example 1 and Example 2 named "/users/{user-token}/bank-accounts".

## Notes
- Ensure `PRIVATE_JWK` is configured in the active environment (Production Paylution).
- Headers must remain `application/jose+json` for both request and response.
- The request currently includes placeholders for query values; these may be provided either in the body (preferred) or as query parameters depending on API behavior.

get.description:
Retrieve details of a specific bank account (transfer method) that belongs to a given user.

### Overview
This endpoint returns the current state and configuration of a single bank account (also referred to as a transfer method) for a user in Hyperwallet. It is typically used to:

- Display a user’s registered payout bank account in your UI
- Verify that a bank account is active/verified before creating or scheduling a payment
- Retrieve compliance- and banking‑related attributes for audit or troubleshooting

The request is signed (JWS) and encrypted (JWE) by the pre‑request script before it is sent to the Hyperwallet API.

### Path and key identifiers
Although concrete IDs are hard‑coded in the sample URL for demonstration, conceptually the resource follows this pattern:

- `user-token` (`usr-…`): Unique, auto‑generated identifier of the user who owns the bank account.
- `bank-account-token` (`trm-…`): Unique, auto‑generated identifier of the bank account / transfer method.

The sample URL in this request uses fixed `usr-…` and `trm-…` values so you can run it directly. In production you should replace them with the appropriate user and transfer‑method tokens from your environment or variables.

### Query parameters
This request includes a comprehensive set of optional query parameters that mirror the fields of a Hyperwallet bank account. Commonly used parameters include:

- `token`: Bank account (transfer method) token.
- `status`: Bank account status (for example: `ACTIVATED`, `VERIFIED`, `INVALID`, `DE_ACTIVATED`).
- `type`: Transfer method type, such as `BANK_ACCOUNT` (direct deposit) or `WIRE_ACCOUNT` (wire transfer).
- `transferMethodCountry` / `transferMethodCurrency`: Country and currency of the bank account.
- `isDefaultTransferMethod`: Indicates whether this is the user’s default payout method.
- Holder details such as `firstName`, `lastName`, `profileType` (`INDIVIDUAL` or `BUSINESS`), `addressLine1`, `city`, `stateProvince`, `country`, and `postalCode`.
- Business details such as `businessName`, `businessType`, and business registration fields.
- Banking details such as `bankAccountId`, `bankAccountPurpose`, `bankId`, `bankName`, `branchId`, and branch address fields.
- Wire‑specific and intermediary‑bank fields (for `WIRE_ACCOUNT`), including `intermediaryBankId`, `intermediaryBankAccountId`, and `wireInstructions`.

The included example values are illustrative. Adjust or remove query parameters as needed for your specific integration or to reproduce particular scenarios.

### Authentication and headers
This request uses HTTP Basic authentication at the request level (username/password for your Hyperwallet API user) and relies on a pre‑request script to apply JWS signing and JWE encryption:

- **Auth**: Basic Auth (Hyperwallet API username and password).
- **Content-Type**: `application/jose+json`
- **Accept**: `application/jose+json`

The pre‑request script:

1. Builds a JWS using your private key (`PRIVATE_JWK` in the active environment) to sign the payload.
2. Encrypts the signed payload into a compact JWE using Hyperwallet’s public encryption key obtained from the JWKS endpoint (`HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL`).
3. Replaces the raw request body with the final JWE compact representation before the request is sent.

Ensure the following environment variables are configured:

- `PRIVATE_JWK`: Your RSA private key in JWK format used to sign the JWS.
- `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL`: URL for retrieving Hyperwallet’s JWKS set (defaults to `https://api.paylution.com/jwkset` if not set).

### Responses
Typical responses include:

- **200 OK** – Bank account retrieved successfully. The response payload (decrypted by your client or helper utilities) contains the bank account details, including token, status, transfer‑method type, currency, and KYC‑related attributes.
- **401 Unauthorized** – Authentication failed (for example, incorrect Basic Auth credentials). See the example response in this collection for the `INCORRECT_LOGIN_CREDENTIALS` error.
- **403 Forbidden** – The credentials are valid but do not have access to the specified user or bank account.
- **404 Not Found** – The specified `user-token` or `bank-account-token` does not exist or is not associated.
- **4xx Validation errors** – One or more parameters are invalid or not supported for your program.

Use the saved examples associated with this request to explore the exact response structure and error payloads returned by the Hyperwallet API.

put.description:
### Overview
This endpoint updates an existing bank account associated with a specific user in Hyperwallet.

- **HTTP method:** `PUT`
- **Path:** `/users/{user-token}/bank-accounts/{bank-account-token}`
- **Content type:** `application/jose+json` (JWE/JWS wrapped payload)

Use this operation to modify stored details for a user’s bank account (for example, updating the underlying bank account identifier).

---
### Path parameters
- `user-token` (string, required)
  - Unique token of the user who owns the bank account.
  - Must reference an existing user in Hyperwallet.

- `bank-account-token` (string, required)
  - Unique token of the bank account to be updated.
  - Must reference an existing bank account belonging to the specified user.

---
### Query parameters
Unless otherwise specified by your Hyperwallet integration, these query parameters are typically used as alternative ways to pass the same values that are contained in the encrypted body. In most integrations they are either omitted or left blank, and the JWE/JWS payload is the source of truth.

- `user-token` (string, optional)
  - User token; should match the path-level `user-token` when used.

- `bank-account-token` (string, optional)
  - Bank account token; should match the path-level `bank-account-token` when used.

- `profileType` (string, optional)
  - User profile type (e.g. `INDIVIDUAL`, `BUSINESS`).

- `transferMethodCurrency` (string, optional)
  - Currency code (ISO 4217, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`) for this bank account transfer method.

- `branchId` (string, optional)
  - Bank branch identifier (e.g. routing code, sort code, or local equivalent).

- `bankAccountId` (string, optional)
  - Bank account number or local account identifier. Typically should match the `bankAccountId` in the request body when both are provided.

- `bankAccountPurpose` (string, optional)
  - Describes the intended purpose of the account (e.g. `CHECKING`, `SAVINGS`, or country-specific values).

- `firstName`, `middleName`, `lastName` (string, optional)
  - Name fields for the bank account holder. Should match the user’s registered profile where applicable.

- `country` (string, optional)
  - Country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. `US`, `CA`).

- `stateProvince` (string, optional)
  - State or province, when applicable for the specified country.

- `addressLine1`, `addressLine2` (string, optional)
  - Street address fields for the bank account holder.

- `city` (string, optional)
  - City of the bank account holder’s address.

- `postalCode` (string, optional)
  - Postal or ZIP code of the bank account holder’s address.

---
### Request body
The body must be sent as a JWE/JWS wrapped JSON object (content type `application/jose+json`). The encrypted payload, once decrypted by Hyperwallet, typically includes:

- Identification of the bank account being updated
- Updated account holder information
- Updated bank routing and account fields

Example (pre-encryption, conceptual only):

```json
{
  "bankAccountId": "7845012345"
}
```

> Note: The actual payload you send to Hyperwallet must be wrapped in a signed JWS and then encrypted as a JWE according to your integration’s security configuration. The cleartext JSON above is for illustration only and is never sent directly.

---
### Security
This endpoint requires:

- A valid Hyperwallet API program configuration.
- JWS signing using your private key.
- JWE encryption using Hyperwallet’s public key (retrieved from their JWKS endpoint).

Ensure that:

- The `alg`, `kid`, and related JOSE header fields match your program configuration.
- The decrypted payload is consistent with the path and query parameters (e.g. `userToken`, `bankAccountId`).

---
### Typical use cases
- Updating a user’s bank account number while keeping the same bank account token.
- Correcting account holder details (name, address) for compliance reasons.
- Updating account purpose or related metadata while keeping the transfer method active.

---
### Error handling
Common error scenarios include:

- **400 Bad Request** – Invalid or missing fields in the decrypted payload, or inconsistent values between the payload and the path/query parameters.
- **401/403 Unauthorized/Forbidden** – Missing or invalid authentication, or JOSE signature/encryption issues.
- **404 Not Found** – Specified user or bank account token does not exist or does not belong to the user.
- **409 Conflict** – Business rule violations (e.g. attempting to modify an account in a non-modifiable state).

Errors are returned as encrypted responses, which you should decrypt to inspect the underlying JSON error structure.

---
### Decrypted response examples

#### 200 OK – Bank account updated (decrypted JSON)
```json
{
  "token": "trm-54a9c571-602a-4592-b7a1-f378026a7205",
  "userToken": "usr-4a3658f5-1fdc-4553-b2da-0b69c195c5ac",
  "type": "BANK_ACCOUNT",
  "status": "ACTIVATED",
  "profileType": "INDIVIDUAL",
  "transferMethodCurrency": "USD",
  "transferMethodCountry": "US",

  "bankName": "Example Bank",
  "branchId": "021000021",
  "bankAccountId": "7845012345",
  "bankAccountPurpose": "CHECKING",

  "firstName": "John",
  "middleName": "A",
  "lastName": "Doe",
  "country": "US",
  "stateProvince": "CA",
  "addressLine1": "123 Market Street",
  "addressLine2": "Suite 500",
  "city": "San Francisco",
  "postalCode": "94105",

  "verificationStatus": "VERIFIED",
  "createdOn": "2024-08-15T10:12:34Z",
  "updatedOn": "2024-09-01T09:30:00Z",

  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "self",
      "href": "https://api.paylution.com/users/usr-4a3658f5-1fdc-4553-b2da-0b69c195c5ac/bank-accounts/trm-54a9c571-602a-4592-b7a1-f378026a7205",
      "method": "GET"

    {
      "rel": "deactivate",
      "href": "https://api.paylution.com/users/usr-4a3658f5-1fdc-4553-b2da-0b69c195c5ac/bank-accounts/trm-54a9c571-602a-4592-b7a1-f378026a7205",
```

#### 400 Bad Request – Validation error (decrypted JSON)

```json
    {
```

Creates a bank card transfer method for an existing Hyperwallet user.

### Overview

This endpoint creates and registers a bank card (e.g. debit/credit card) as a transfer method for the specified user. The request payload is signed as a JWS and then encrypted as a JWE by the existing pre-request script before being sent to Hyperwallet.

### Path

- `user-token` (path): The unique token of the user for whom the bank card transfer method is being created. It appears in the URL as `/users/{user-token}/bank-cards`.


### Query Parameters (current URL)

These are currently present in the request URL and may be used by some integrations. They are typically not required when the same values are provided in the JSON body.

- `user-token` (query): Optional. User token; usually supplied as a path variable instead.

- `type` (query): Optional. Transfer method type (e.g. `BANK_CARD`).

- `transferMethodCountry` (query): Optional. 2-letter ISO country code for the transfer method (e.g. `US`).

- `transferMethodCurrency` (query): Optional. 3-letter ISO currency code for the transfer method (e.g. `USD`).

- `cardNumber` (query): Optional. Bank card number.

- `cvv` (query): Optional. Card security code.


### Headers

- `Content-Type`: Typically `application/jose+json`. Indicates that the request body is a JWE-wrapped JWS JSON payload.

- `Accept`: Typically `application/jose+json`. Indicates the client expects a JWE-wrapped JWS JSON response.


### JSON Body

Raw JSON is authored in the request, then the pre-request script:

1. Signs the JSON as a JWS using the configured private key.

2. Encrypts the JWS as a JWE using the Hyperwallet JWKS.


Fields in the body before signing/encryption:

- `cardNumber` (string): Full primary account number of the bank card (e.g. `"440353001767298"`).

- `dateOfExpiry` (string): Card expiry in `YYYY-MM` format (e.g. `"2027-11"`).

- `cvv` (string): Card security code (e.g. `"683"`).

- `transferMethodCountry` (string): 2-letter ISO country code for the card (e.g. `"US"`).

- `transferMethodCurrency` (string): 3-letter ISO currency code for the card (e.g. `"USD"`).

- `type` (string): Transfer method type. For this endpoint it is typically `"BANK_CARD"`.


---

### Examples

The following examples describe the **decrypted JSON payload** that the pre-request/post-response scripts expose via `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` after JWE/JWS processing. These are **not** the raw JOSE envelopes sent over the wire.

#### 1. Successful bank card creation (201/200-style)

On success, Hyperwallet returns a bank card transfer method resource. After decryption, `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` typically has a structure similar to:

``` json
{
  "token": "trm-12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-1234567890ab",
  "type": "BANK_CARD",
  "status": "ACTIVATED",
  "cardNumber": "************7298",
  "dateOfExpiry": "2027-11",
  "transferMethodCountry": "US",
  "transferMethodCurrency": "USD",
  "userToken": "usr-ff57e5f6-f6b0-4bc4-aa6a-6b9d0af5e6ca",
  "createdOn": "2024-01-15T10:23:45Z",
  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "self",
      "href": "https://api.paylution.com/rest/v4/users/usr-ff57e5f6-f6b0-4bc4-aa6a-6b9d0af5e6ca/bank-cards/trm-12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-1234567890ab",
      "method": "GET"
    },
    {
      "rel": "deactivate",
      "href": "https://api.paylution.com/rest/v4/users/usr-ff57e5f6-f6b0-4bc4-aa6a-6b9d0af5e6ca/bank-cards/trm-12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-1234567890ab/de-status",
      "method": "PUT"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

Key points:

- `cardNumber` is usually masked in the response.

- `status` reflects the current state of the transfer method (e.g. `ACTIVATED`, `DE_ACTIVATED`).

- `links` provides HATEOAS-style navigation and operations for this transfer method.


#### 2. Typical validation/business error

For validation or business errors (e.g. invalid card number, expired card, unsupported currency), the decrypted payload usually follows Hyperwallet's standard error format:

``` json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "BANK_CARD_VALIDATION_ERROR",
      "message": "The bank card number is invalid.",
      "fieldName": "cardNumber"
    }
  ],
  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "self",
      "href": "https://api.paylution.com/rest/v4/users/usr-ff57e5f6-f6b0-4bc4-aa6a-6b9d0af5e6ca/bank-cards",
      "method": "POST"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

Characteristics:

- One or more `errors` entries may be present.

- `code` is a machine-readable error identifier.

- `message` is human readable and may be localized.

- `fieldName` (when present) points to the offending request field.


---

### Decrypted Response Schema

The following schema describes the **application-level JSON** placed into `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` by the decryption logic in the post-response script. It does **not** describe the outer JWE/JWS envelope, which remains opaque to the collection user.

Depending on the outcome, the decrypted payload will be either a **bank card transfer method resource** or an **error container**.

#### Success payload (bank card transfer method)

``` jsonc
{
  "token": "string",                 // Transfer method token (e.g. "trm-...")
  "type": "string",                  // Expected: "BANK_CARD"
  "status": "string",                // e.g. "ACTIVATED", "DE_ACTIVATED", "PRE_ACTIVATED"
  "cardNumber": "string",            // Masked PAN, e.g. "************7298"
  "dateOfExpiry": "string",          // YYYY-MM
  "transferMethodCountry": "string", // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "US"
  "transferMethodCurrency": "string",// ISO 4217, e.g. "USD"
  "userToken": "string",             // Owning user token, e.g. "usr-..."
  "createdOn": "string",             // ISO 8601 timestamp of creation
  "links": [                          // Optional but usually present
    {
      "rel": "string",              // Relationship, e.g. "self", "deactivate"
      "href": "string",             // Absolute URL for the link
      "method": "string"            // HTTP method, e.g. "GET", "PUT"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

Fields are indicative; exact presence and values may vary based on Hyperwallet configuration and lifecycle state.

#### Error payload

``` jsonc
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "string",        // Machine-readable code, e.g. "BANK_CARD_VALIDATION_ERROR"
      "message": "string",     // Human-readable message
      "fieldName": "string"    // (Optional) Field the error relates to, e.g. "cardNumber"
    }
  ],
  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "string",        // Usually "self"
      "href": "string",       // Endpoint URL that produced the error
      "method": "string"      // e.g. "POST"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

Again, this schema reflects the structure of the **decrypted** JSON that the test script parses from `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD`, not the encrypted/signed JOSE wrapper returned on the wire.

get.description:
### Get Bank Card Details

Retrieves details for a specific bank card that belongs to a given user.

This endpoint is typically used to:
- Display a user’s registered bank card details (for review/verification)
- Check card attributes such as status, brand, type, expiry, and default-transfer-method flag

#### HTTP Request
`GET {{base_url}}/users/{user-token}/bank-cards/{bank-card-token}`

- `{{base_url}}` is provided by the active environment.
- `user-token` uniquely identifies the user.
- `bank-card-token` uniquely identifies the bank card belonging to that user.

#### Path Parameters
- `user-token` (required) — The user’s unique token.
- `bank-card-token` (required) — The unique token of the bank card associated with the user.

#### Query Parameters
All query parameters are optional filters/attributes that may be included by the API but are usually not required for a simple lookup.

- `token` — Bank card token filter.
- `status` — Card status (for example, `ACTIVATED`, `DEACTIVATED`, etc.).
- `createdOn` — Creation date/time filter.
- `type` — Bank card type or category.
- `transferMethodCountry` — ISO country code of the transfer method.
- `transferMethodCurrency` — ISO currency code of the transfer method.
- `isDefaultTransferMethod` — Indicates whether this is the default transfer method.
- `cardBrand` — Card brand (for example, `VISA`, `MASTERCARD`).
- `cardNumber` — Masked or partial card number filter.
- `cardType` — Card type (for example, `DEBIT`, `CREDIT`).
- `dateOfExpiry` — Card expiry date filter.

#### Authentication & Security (JWS / JWE)
This endpoint expects:
- **Signed request payload (JWS)** using your private signing key.
- **Encrypted payload (JWE)** using Hyperwallet’s published JWKS.

The pre-request script for this request:
- Fetches the encryption key from `HYPERWALLET_JWKS_URL` (or the default JWKS endpoint).
- Uses `PRIVATE_JWK` / `PRIVATE_JWK_SIG` from the active environment to sign the payload.
- Produces a JWS, then encrypts it into a JWE and sets the request body/headers accordingly (even for GET requests, as required by Hyperwallet’s security model).

**Required headers** (already configured):
- `Content-Type: application/jose+json`
- `Accept: application/jose+json`

Ensure the environment variables for your private keys and JWKS URL are correctly set before sending the request.

#### Responses
Typical behavior (see saved examples for full wire-level details):

- **200 OK** — Bank card details successfully retrieved. The encrypted response body (JWE) is decrypted by the collection utilities and stored as `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` in the environment. The post-response script validates that:
  - `payload.links` is present.
  - `payload.processingTime` is present.

- **4xx Client Errors** — Validation, authorization, or not-found issues, such as:
  - Missing/invalid `user-token` or `bank-card-token`.
  - Invalid or expired credentials / signature / encryption.
  - Bank card not found for the specified user.

- **5xx Server Errors** — Transient or internal server issues in the upstream Hyperwallet service.

Use the saved examples for this request to understand specific status codes, response shapes, and query parameter combinations.

## Overview

Retrieves the collection of PayPal transfer methods (PayPal accounts) associated with a specific Hyperwallet user. Use this endpoint to inspect which PayPal account(s) a user has registered, determine the default PayPal transfer method before initiating a payout, and page through historical or multiple PayPal accounts linked to the same user.

The resource is exposed at `/users/{user-token}/PayPal-accounts` and returns a paginated list of PayPal transfer methods for the specified user.

## Authentication

This operation uses Hyperwallet’s JOSE-based security model. On the wire, both request and response are transported as signed JWS wrapped in encrypted JWE:

- **Content-Type**: `application/jose+json`
- **Accept**: `application/jose+json`

The pre-request script signs the logical request payload and encrypts it using the Hyperwallet public key. The response is decrypted by the collection utilities, and the clear-text JSON is stored in `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` for inspection and testing. The examples and tests attached to this request describe the **decrypted JSON** shape, not the raw JWE/JWS envelope.

## Path Parameters

- `user-token`  
  - **Required**  
  - Hyperwallet user token (for example: `usr-6243d549-be97-486d-ac0f-385dec42ebb4`).  
  - Identifies the user whose PayPal transfer methods you want to list.

## Query Parameters

All query parameters are optional. When omitted, the endpoint returns the first page of PayPal accounts for the specified user.

- `token`  
  - Filter by a specific PayPal transfer method token (for example: `trm-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`).
- `accountId`  
  - Filter by the PayPal account identifier for the user (email address, phone number, or payer ID as stored in Hyperwallet).
- `status`  
  - Filter by transfer method status (for example: `ACTIVATED`, `VERIFIED`, `INVALID`, `DE_ACTIVATED`), depending on your program configuration.
- `type`  
  - Filter by transfer method type. For this resource the value is typically `PAYPAL_ACCOUNT`.
- `transferMethodCountry`  
  - Restrict results to PayPal accounts configured for a specific country (ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2, such as `US`, `GB`).
- `transferMethodCurrency`  
  - Restrict results to PayPal accounts for a specific currency (ISO 4217, such as `USD`, `EUR`).
- `isDefaultTransferMethod`  
  - When `true`, returns only the default PayPal transfer method for the user; when `false`, returns only non-default transfer methods.
- `createdBefore`  
  - Returns PayPal accounts created **before** this timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). If only a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is provided, the time portion defaults to `00:00:00`.
- `createdAfter`  
  - Returns PayPal accounts created **after** this timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC). If only a date is provided, the time portion defaults to `00:00:00`.
- `createdOn`  
  - Returns PayPal accounts created **exactly on** this datetime (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `sortBy`  
  - Attribute used to sort the result set. Commonly `createdOn`; by default, results are sorted in ascending order.
- `limit`  
  - Maximum number of records to return in a single page (default `100`, range `1`–`1000`).

## Responses

- **200 OK** – Returns a **paginated list object** containing PayPal transfer methods for the user. The decrypted JSON response typically includes:
  - `count`, `offset`, `limit` – pagination counters.
  - `hasNextPage`, `hasPreviousPage` – paging flags.
  - `data` – array of PayPal transfer method objects (each representing a PayPal account registered for the user).
  - `links` – HATEOAS-style links for navigation (e.g., self, next, previous).

Each PayPal transfer method object in `data` includes fields such as `token`, `type` (`PAYPAL_ACCOUNT`), `status`, `transferMethodCountry`, `transferMethodCurrency`, and related metadata.

## Error Codes

Typical HTTP responses for this operation include:

- **400 Bad Request** – The request is syntactically correct but one or more query parameters are invalid or inconsistent.
- **401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden** – Authentication failed, JOSE credentials are missing/invalid, or the API client is not permitted to access the user’s transfer methods.
- **404 Not Found** – The specified `user-token` does not exist or is not available under your program.
- **409 Conflict** – A conflict was detected when resolving the request (for example, inconsistent filters versus program configuration).
- **429 Too Many Requests** – Rate limit exceeded for the calling program or credentials.
- **5xx Server Error** – An unexpected error occurred in the Hyperwallet/Paylution platform. The operation may be retried according to your resiliency policy.

## Overview

Creates (registers) a new PayPal transfer method (PayPal account) for a specific Hyperwallet user. Once created and activated, this PayPal transfer method can be used as a payout destination for funds sent through your Hyperwallet program.

The resource is exposed at `/users/{user-token}/PayPal-accounts` and represents a single PayPal transfer method owned by the specified user.

## Authentication

This operation uses Hyperwallet’s JOSE-based security model. On the wire, both request and response are transported as signed JWS wrapped in encrypted JWE:

- **Content-Type**: `application/jose+json`

- **Accept**: `application/jose+json`


The pre-request script signs the logical JSON payload and encrypts it using the Hyperwallet public key. The response is decrypted by the collection utilities, and the clear-text JSON is stored in `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` for inspection and testing. The request examples and tests attached here describe the **decrypted JSON** structure, not the raw JWE/JWS envelope.

## Path Parameters

- `user-token`

    - **Required**

    - Hyperwallet user token (for example: `usr-6243d549-be97-486d-ac0f-385dec42ebb4`).

    - Identifies the user who will own the new PayPal transfer method.


## Request Body

Although the actual payload is transmitted as an encrypted JWE, the logical/decrypted request body is a JSON object with the following fields:

- `type` _(string, required)_

    - Transfer method type. For this endpoint the value is typically `PAYPAL_ACCOUNT`.

    - **Example**: `"PAYPAL_ACCOUNT"`

- `accountId` _(string, required)_

    - PayPal account identifier for the user. Commonly the PayPal email address, but may also be a supported phone number or payer ID depending on your program configuration.configuration.

    - **Example**: `"user.paypal@example.com"`

- `transferMethodCountry` _(string, required)_

    - Country where the PayPal account will be used. Must be supported for your program (ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 code).

    - **Example**: `"US"`, `"GB"`

- `transferMethodCurrency` _(string, required)_

    - Currency in which payouts will be made to this PayPal account. Must be supported for your program in combination with the country (ISO 4217 code).

    - **Example**: `"USD"`, `"EUR"`

- `isDefaultTransferMethod` _(boolean or boolean string, optional)_

    - When `true`, marks this PayPal transfer method as the user’s default payout method (subject to program rules and any existing default).

    - **Example**: `true` or `"true"`


## Responses

- **201 Created** – PayPal transfer method successfully created. The decrypted JSON response body represents a single PayPal transfer method object and typically includes:

    - `token` – unique PayPal transfer method token (for example: `trm-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`).

    - `type` – should be `PAYPAL_ACCOUNT`.

    - `status` – current status of the transfer method (for example: `ACTIVATED`, `VERIFIED`, `INVALID`, `DE_ACTIVATED`).

    - `transferMethodCountry`, `transferMethodCurrency` – configured country and currency for payouts.

    - `userToken` – the owning Hyperwallet user token.

    - `isDefaultTransferMethod` – indicates whether this is the default payout method for the user.

    - `links` – HATEOAS-style links to this resource and related operations.


## Error Codes

Typical HTTP responses for this operation include:

- **400 Bad Request** – Validation error, such as invalid `accountId` format, unsupported country/currency combination, or missing required fields in the decrypted JSON body.

- **401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden** – Authentication failed, JOSE credentials are missing/invalid, or the API client is not permitted to create PayPal transfer methods for this user.

- **404 Not Found** – The specified `user-token` does not exist or is not available under your program.

- **409 Conflict** – A PayPal transfer method with the same account details already exists for this user, or the operation conflicts with current program rules.

- **429 Too Many Requests** – Rate limit exceeded for the calling program or crledentials.

- **5xx Server Error** – An unexpected error occurred in the Hyperwallet/Paylution platform. The operation may be retried according to your resiliency policy.


## 1. Purpose of `POST /users/{user-token}/PayPal-accounts`

This endpoint creates/registers a **new PayPal transfer method** for an existing Hyperwallet user.

Typical uses:

- Onboarding flow: user links a new PayPal account to receive payouts

- Account management: add a new PayPal account while keeping existing ones

- Setting a default payout method: mark the new account as the default transfer method


Resource path:  
`POST /users/{user-token}/paypal-accounts`

- `user-token` (path): existing Hyperwallet user token (`usr-…`) for whom you’re adding the PayPal account.


Headers (same JOSE pattern as your GET):

- `Content-Type: application/jose+json` (JWE-wrapped JSON payload you sign/encrypt in the pre-request script)

- `Accept: application/jose+json` (you expect a JWE-wrapped JSON response)


Internally, the decrypted JSON you care about will be in `DECRYPTED_PAYLOAD` (as you already do for the GET).

get.description:
Retrieves a filtered, paginated list of payments for the program.

### Overview
Use this endpoint to search and list payments created in your program. You can filter by creation and release dates, status, amount, destination, and other attributes, and optionally page through results.

### Authentication & Headers
- **Auth**: Inherits authentication from the parent **Hyperwallet Documentation** collection/folder (JWS/JWE signing handled by the pre-request script).
- **Content-Type**: `application/jose+json` (required)
- **Accept**: `application/jose+json` (required)

### Query Parameters
All parameters are optional unless noted otherwise. When omitted, the API uses its defaults.

- `clientPaymentId` (string)
  - Client-defined identifier for the payment. Can be used to search for a specific payment created with this client ID.

- `createdBefore` (datetime, ISO 8601)
  - Returns payments **created before** this timestamp.

- `createdAfter` (datetime, ISO 8601)
  - Returns payments **created after** this timestamp.

- `createdOn` (date, ISO 8601)
  - Returns payments created **on** this specific date.

- `releaseDate` (date, ISO 8601)
  - Returns payments with this scheduled release date.

- `releaseOn` (date, ISO 8601)
  - Alias/variant filter for release date; when provided, returns payments scheduled to release on this date.

- `status` (string)
  - Filters by payment status (for example: `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, etc.).

- `amount` (number)
  - Filters payments by exact amount.

- `currency` (string, ISO 4217)
  - Filters by payment currency (for example: `USD`, `EUR`).

- `destinationToken` (string)
  - Filters by the destination token (e.g., user or transfer method token) associated with the payment.

- `programToken` (string)
  - Filters payments belonging to a specific program.

- `purpose` (string)
  - Filters by business purpose/category of the payment, if configured.

- `expiresOn` (date, ISO 8601)
  - Filters by the date on which the payment expires, if applicable.

- `memo` (string)
  - Filters by memo text stored on the payment.

- `notes` (string)
  - Filters by notes text stored on the payment.

- `sortBy` (string)
  - Sort order for the result set. Typical values include fields such as `createdOn` or `releaseDate`, optionally with direction (e.g., `createdOn desc`).

- `limit` (integer)
  - Maximum number of records to return in a single page of results.

- `token` (string)
  - Pagination cursor/token returned from a previous call. Use this to fetch the **next page** of results.
